title: Best Bike Lights UK
short: Front and rear bike lights compared by lumens, battery life and who they suit, for commuting, road and trail.
intro: Once the clocks change, a decent set of bike lights stops being optional. This guide compares front and rear lights tested by BikeRadar, which says it has tested more than 500 lights over 17 years, so you can pick lights matched to how dark and how fast you ride.

products.name: Blinder 1300
products.best_for: On- and off-road riding where you want one capable light
products.summary: BikeRadar's overall winner. A compact, well-made front light with a low handlebar profile, though it has a relatively short runtime at peak brightness.

products.name: Swift 500
products.summary: A user-friendly, durable and waterproof front light well suited to commuting, though side illumination is limited and BikeRadar found the claimed runtime inaccurate.
cons: Claimed runtime found to be inaccurate

products.name: Macro Drive 1400+
products.best_for: Road cyclists who want strong sustained output
products.summary: A robustly built road light with strong extended high-output performance, though it has fewer customisation options than some rivals.

products.name: Sirius Mk10 Daybright
products.best_for: Riders who prioritise being seen over maximum brightness
products.summary: A premium, compact light with a practical beam designed for visibility, though mode switching is more complex and it uses a proprietary charging cable.
products.search: Exposure Sirius Mk10 Daybright bike light

products.name: Ray 2600B Smart Remote
products.best_for: Off-road and gravel riding in the dark
products.summary: A very bright light suited to trail brightness needs, with an extended runtime and a handlebar remote, though BikeRadar found the companion app unreliable.
products.search: Magicshine Ray 2600B Smart Remote bike light

products.name: Strip Drive Pro 400+
products.best_for: Riders who want strong, visible output with several modes
products.summary: BikeRadar's top rear light. Powerful output with seven mode options and a memory function, though the charging cable is not included.
products.search: Lezyne Strip Drive Pro 400+ rear bike light

products.name: Buster RL 150
products.summary: A compact, straightforward rear light with a brake detection mode, at a budget-friendly price, though its output is only moderate.
products.search: Sigma Buster RL 150 rear bike light

products.name: TR250
products.best_for: Riders who want auto-on and brake alert features at a reasonable price
products.key_spec: 250 lumens, up to 18.5hr battery, brake function
products.summary: A rear light with responsive brake activation, auto-on capability and multiple mounting options, offering strong value for the features included.
cons: Runtime can be variable depending on riding style

guide.q: How many lumens do I need?
guide.a: For daytime visibility, 100-plus lumen front and rear lights are generally sufficient. For urban riding in the dark with some street lighting, aim for at least 400 lumens at the front. For unlit roads at night, look for 600 lumens or more.

guide.q: Front and rear, or do I only need one?
guide.a: UK law requires a white front light and a red rear light after dark, so you need both, even if the front light is far more powerful than the rear.

Both are legal in the UK. Flashing mode saves battery and can attract more attention in daylight or dusk, while steady mode helps other road users judge your distance and speed more accurately in full darkness.

guide.q: What is brake detection on a rear light?
guide.a: Some rear lights sense when you slow down and automatically brighten, similar to a car brake light, which can make you more visible to traffic behind you when you decelerate.
